data.title: Alpine Visitor Center
data.description: Alpine Visitor Center, located at the top of Fall River Pass, is at an elevation of 11,796 feet above sea level. This is the highest elevation visitor center in the national park system. This webcam shows views of alpine tundra along with Mount Chapin, Fall River Canyon and Old Fall River Road.

data.title: Kawuneeche Valley
data.description: Located on the west side of Rocky Mountain National Park, the Kawuneeche Valley is home to a variety of flora and fauna. This webcam shows views of Harbison Meadow, located 0.5-miles north of the Grand Lake Entrance. Enjoy views of the Never Summer Mountains in the distance.

data.title: Longs Peak
data.description: Longs Peak towers over all other peaks in Rocky Mountain National Park at an elevation of 14,259 feet above sea level. It is a challenging mountain to climb under the best conditions. This webcam shows views of Longs Peak as seen from the Tahosa Valley.

data.title: Fall River Entrance/U.S. Hwy 34
data.description: Fall River Entrance is located just west of the Town of Estes Park on U.S. Highway 34. This view is looking east from the entrance station, depicting the flow of vehicles entering the park.

data.title: Beaver Meadows Entrance/U.S. Hwy 36
data.description: Beaver Meadows Entrance is located just west of the Town of Estes Park on U.S. Highway 36. This view is looking east from the entrance station, depicting the flow of vehicles entering the park.

data.title: Grand Lake Entrance/ U.S. Hwy 34
data.description: Grand Lake Entrance is located on the west side of Rocky Mountain National Park on U.S. Highway 34/Trail Ridge Road just north of the Town of Grand Lake. This view is looking south from the entrance station, depicting the flow of vehicles entering the park.

data.title: Continental Divide
data.description: The Continental Divide Webcam offers a spectacular view of a meadow near Glacier Basin Campground and stunning mountain peaks in the distance. On a clear day, enjoy views of Thatchtop, Taylor Peak, Otis Peak, and Hallett Peak.
